Wrong answers tended to focus on benefits to the business or offered examples of possible external benefits. Others made vague references to people which could not be accepted. (b) Many candidates were able to gain at least one mark for identifying ways including limiting where or when a business could operate. A common mistake was to identify the legal control, rather than focus on the effect of it on a business. Other answers wrongly identified legal controls relating to employees or marketing, rather than location. (c) Good knowledge was evident in most responses.
